usa_mod.why: a mod made over the North American disc as the importer writes one (a real USA crate's import row: the North American archive's size and hashes, no game data): ON, and on this European disc the base check leaves it out at the start -- the census does not count it, the start-up log line names the region; the base drew 'made for the north american disc' under its row. Its recipe is the identity over this disc's archive (base 0 <the disc's CRASH6/CRASH.BD size>), so a game that composed it anyway would read the disc's own bytes

page.left_out_log: mods: the disc overlay left out usa_left_out: it was made for the North American disc, and this is the European disc (
page.why: the route walks title -> main menu -> options -> mods, one row down and CROSS. The mods folder holds the order pair (order_a, order_b: ON, switched in the launcher -- the settings file), the code-changes mod (OFF), a North American mod (ON, left out on this disc by the base check) and the Arabic language pack (an earlier version's switch on, first in mods.order). The page lists ONLY the mods that apply while the game runs: 'level select' and 'speedrun mode : off|on' -- no folder mod's name, no note, nothing about the pack, and no other '<name> : off|on' row; the second row is speedrun mode, and CROSS switches it on at once (the log, the row reads 'speedrun mode : on', the settings file gets mods.speedrun.enabled = on). Nothing in the game writes a folder mod's key: the launcher's lines are as they were and none is added. The start-up log keeps the left-out line

applied.why: the overlays the launcher switched on still apply in the same run: the OPTIONS page the route passes draws order_b's line (mods.order puts order_b last: 'graphic optionb', and its 'sound optionz'), never the disc's 'graphic options'; the census row counts two layers (the left-out mod is not one)

base_route.why: the vanilla run of the OPTIONS route (no settings file, no mods folder) draws the disc's 'graphic options' (the route reaches the page): the reference for 'applied'
